C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-202.Summary:
Deliver the second bounded M1.3 browser-service slice by adding independent downloads and cookies/site-data service plugins above the existing M1.2 browser engine primitives.
The downloads service owns durable product-level download records and artifact identity without exposing provider staging paths as filesystem authority.
The cookies service separates metadata inspection, secret-value disclosure, mutation and service policy while leaving Chromium's profile cookie store authoritative for actual cookie values.
All new service contracts remain experimental version 0.1. Stable Browser Contract v1.0 remains wire-compatible.

Goals.Goal: Extend the existing engine-neutral browser-services contract crate with experimental browser.downloads/0.1, browser.cookies/0.1 and the minimum browser.site-data/0.1 surface justified by existing engine primitives.
Implement an ordinary downloads plugin with durable DownloadRecordId identity, lifecycle state, progress/reconciliation metadata and completed artifact references independent from engine DownloadId.
Ensure completed download content is represented to service consumers by an opaque artifact/blob reference rather than a host filesystem path.
Implement an ordinary cookies service that exposes metadata inspection separately from raw cookie-value access and mutation.
Implement bounded site-data clearing over existing context/origin-scoped storage primitives without exposing Chromium profile files or databases.
Persist service-owned policy and durable product records while preserving Chromium profile storage as the source of truth for cookie values and engine-managed site data.
Prove crash/restart reconciliation and optional-service failure isolation through a bounded S3B proving slice.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL REMAIN SEPARATE; THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
C-BROWSER-TABS-HISTORY-SERVICES-20260901 MUST REMAIN APPLIED AND ARCHIVED BEFORE THIS CHANGE'S PLAN IS APPROVED OR EXECUTED.
DOWNLOADS, COOKIES AND SITE-DATA SERVICES ARE ORDINARY PLUGINS. NO PRODUCT POLICY OR PRODUCT TYPE MAY ENTER THE KERNEL.
STABLE Browser Contract v1.0 REQUEST/RESPONSE WIRE FORMS, INCLUDING browser.download/v1.0, MUST REMAIN COMPATIBLE.
EXISTING STABLE BROWSER EVENTS MUST NOT RECEIVE REQUIRED NEW FIELDS.
EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL engine.cookies/0.1, engine.storage/0.1 AND engine.download_hook/0.1 MUST NOT BE INCOMPATIBLY REDEFINED IN PLACE.
IF A SAFER ENGINE DOWNLOAD ARTIFACT/HANDOFF SURFACE IS REQUIRED, IT MUST BE AN ADDITIVE OPERATION OR A SEPARATELY VERSIONED EXPERIMENTAL REVISION SUCH AS 0.2, WITH 0.1 FIXTURES PRESERVED.
NEW PRODUCT SERVICE CONTRACTS START AS EXPERIMENTAL 0.1 AND MUST NOT CLAIM V1 STABILITY.
DOWNLOAD PATH TEXT IS DATA, NOT FILESYSTEM AUTHORITY.
THE DOWNLOADS SERVICE MUST NOT EXPOSE PROVIDER STAGING PATHS, CEF PATHS, TEMPORARY FILE LOCATIONS OR HOST-LOCAL FILESYSTEM STRUCTURE AS ITS PRODUCT CONTRACT.
POSSESSION OF DownloadRecordId, DownloadId, ArtifactRef OR BLOB IDENTITY ALONE MUST NOT CONFER READ, WRITE, CONTROL OR EXPORT AUTHORITY.
FINAL EXPORT TO AN ARBITRARY USER FILESYSTEM DESTINATION IS OUT OF SCOPE UNLESS AN EXISTING GENERIC AUTHORIZED FILE/SINK CAPABILITY ALREADY PROVIDES THAT AUTHORITY.
DOWNLOAD START OR CONTROL MUST NOT USE THE SERVICE AS A CONFUSED DEPUTY TO BYPASS PageId OR DownloadId AUTHORIZATION.
NON-IDEMPOTENT DOWNLOAD OPERATIONS MUST NOT BE AUTOMATICALLY RETRIED AFTER AN UNKNOWN EXTERNAL OUTCOME.
ACTUAL COOKIE VALUES REMAIN AUTHORITATIVE IN THE ENGINE PROFILE COOKIE STORE; THE COOKIES SERVICE MUST NOT MAINTAIN A SECOND COOKIE DATABASE.
COOKIE METADATA READ AUTHORITY MUST NOT IMPLY COOKIE VALUE READ AUTHORITY.
COOKIE VALUE READ AUTHORITY MUST NOT IMPLY COOKIE MUTATION AUTHORITY.
COOKIE MUTATION AUTHORITY MUST NOT IMPLY SITE-DATA CLEAR AUTHORITY.
RAW COOKIE VALUES MUST NEVER ENTER GENERIC METRICS, TRAJECTORY, DIAGNOSTIC TEXT, PANIC TEXT, ORDINARY DEBUG OUTPUT OR SERVICE EVENTS.
SERVICE CONTRACT TYPES CARRYING COOKIE SECRETS MUST HAVE REDACTED DEBUG REPRESENTATION OR AN EQUIVALENT MECHANISM THAT PREVENTS ACCIDENTAL PLAINTEXT DEBUG LOGGING.
COOKIE AND SITE-DATA OPERATIONS MUST VALIDATE EXACT BrowserContextId OWNERSHIP AND CANONICAL URL/ORIGIN/DOMAIN SCOPE; STRING SUFFIX MATCHING IS NOT AN AUTHORIZATION RULE.
CROSS-PROFILE OR CROSS-CONTEXT COOKIE/SITE-DATA ACCESS IS DENIED EVEN WHEN HOSTNAMES OR ORIGINS MATCH.
NETWORK-TIME THIRD-PARTY COOKIE FILTERING OR REQUEST INTERCEPTION IS NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE; THAT BELONGS TO THE REQUEST-POLICY BUNDLE.
EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC. DOWNLOAD CONTROL AND COOKIE/SITE-DATA MUTATION ARE CAPABILITY RPC OPERATIONS; EVENTS REPORT FACTS ONLY AFTER OUTCOME.
ALL DURABLE SERVICE STATE USES A DECLARED TRANSACTIONAL SOURCE OF TRUTH; THE EVENT JOURNAL IS NOT DOWNLOAD OR COOKIE-POLICY STATE.
TEST AND PROVING NETWORK CONTENT IS LOCAL/LOOPBACK AND DOES NOT REQUIRE PUBLIC INTERNET ACCESS.
PROTECTED M0, M1.1, M1.2 AND EXISTING M1.3 TABS/HISTORY TESTS ARE NOT WEAKENED OR SKIPPED TO MAKE THIS CHANGE GREEN.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Worldline Shell or final downloads/cookies UI.
Opening downloaded files through OS shell integration.
Password storage, autofill or credential management.
Direct IndexedDB inspection or arbitrary database access.
Duplicating Chromium cookie/storage databases into Worldline state.
Promoting new M1.3 service contracts to stable v1.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: docs/adr/ADR-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS-V1.md is extended, or a bounded downloads/cookies companion ADR is added, documenting authority, persistence, sensitive-data, artifact and reconciliation semantics without reopening the accepted M1.3 plugin architecture.

worldline-browser-services-contract adds engine-neutral experimental browser.downloads/0.1 and browser.cookies/0.1 contracts and only the browser.site-data/0.1 operations justified by implemented engine primitives.
The service-contract crate remains independent from CEF, CDP, Chromium structs, HWND, provider-private implementations and host filesystem paths.
Contract compatibility tests prove stable Browser Contract v1.0 fixtures remain unchanged and all existing experimental engine 0.1 fixtures remain decodable/accepted.
Any required evolution of engine.download_hook is introduced additively or as a separately negotiated experimental revision and is covered by explicit 0.1-to-new-version compatibility tests.
Downloads service defines opaque DownloadRecordId identity independent from engine DownloadId.

The durable download record contains only product-relevant bounded metadata such as originating PageId, URL, suggested filename, media type, byte counts, lifecycle status, engine DownloadId where known and an optional opaque completed-artifact reference.
Durable download records do not persist raw staging paths or arbitrary host filesystem destinations.

Downloads service defines explicit lifecycle states covering at least pending/start, active, paused, completed, cancelled, failed and unknown/incomplete outcome where external completion cannot be proven.
A download intent/record is durably established before issuing a non-idempotent engine start operation, with correlation metadata sufficient for post-crash reconciliation.
If engine start may have occurred but RPC completion is lost, the service records an explicit incomplete/reconciling state and does not automatically issue a second start.
Re-delivered engine download facts or repeated reconciliation do not create duplicate logical DownloadRecordId records.
Service restart reconciles every non-terminal download against the engine where its current outcome is knowable and preserves explicit uncertainty where it is not.
Download pause/resume/cancel require explicit service control authority scoped to the target DownloadRecordId and cannot control another caller's record merely by guessing an engine DownloadId.
Starting a download for a PageId cannot cause the service to manufacture page or engine authority absent an admitted delegated/authorized path.

A deterministic completed download is materialized through the existing generic host blob/artifact mechanism or a generic additive extension to it; browser-service consumers receive an opaque artifact reference rather than a path.
Reading completed artifact bytes requires an independent generic blob/ artifact read authorization; a principal possessing only download-read authority cannot read the content bytes.
Completed artifact content is content-verified in acceptance evidence against deterministic fixture bytes or hash.
Downloads-service crash does not terminate or deadlock the browser engine, existing pages, tabs or history services.
Cookies service exposes distinct authority classes for metadata inspection, secret-value disclosure, mutation and service-policy administration.
Cookie metadata DTOs contain no raw cookie value.

Cookie-value responses use a sensitive value representation whose Debug or equivalent diagnostic formatting is redacted while authorized wire serialization still returns the value to the admitted caller.
A metadata-only principal can enumerate authorized cookie names/domain/ path/security metadata but cannot obtain raw values through response, error, event, metric or debug side channel.
Cookie mutation validates BrowserContextId and canonical selector scope before invoking the engine primitive.
Context A cannot inspect, read, mutate or delete cookies belonging to Context B even when both contexts visit the same loopback origin.
Cookie service does not persist cookie values as its authoritative state; restart reloads actual cookie contents from the engine profile store.
Service-owned cookie access/policy configuration, if implemented in this slice, is persisted independently from the actual cookie store and cannot grant engine authority.
The scope and limits of cookie policy are explicit: this change may govern service-mediated inspection/mutation behavior but does not claim network-time third-party-cookie enforcement.
browser.site-data/0.1 exposes only context/origin-scoped clearing supported by the existing engine.storage primitive and requires separate destructive authority.
Site-data clear canonicalizes the target origin, rejects non-origin or privileged scheme ambiguity, and cannot clear another context's storage.

Clearing origin storage does not implicitly delete unrelated download records, history, tabs or cookies unless the exact requested storage class semantically includes them and that behavior is documented/tested.
Cookie values, authorization data and downloaded content bytes never enter generic browser-service metrics or ordinary events.
Service events contain only bounded post-outcome facts such as download record lifecycle changes or cookie-policy configuration changes and never act as command dispatch.
Static architecture checks prove worldline-kernel and worldline-browser-cef do not depend on DownloadRecordId, browser cookies product policy or the downloads/cookies service implementations.
BrowserServices CI is extended with downloads/cookies contract, authority, persistence, privacy, recovery and failure-isolation tests.

One bounded S3B path against the real M1.2 provider downloads deterministic loopback content, produces a durable DownloadRecordId and authorized artifact reference, verifies bytes, restarts the downloads service and preserves the completed record.
The same S3B path proves a principal with download metadata authority but no artifact-read authority cannot obtain completed bytes.

S3B creates two isolated browser contexts for the same loopback origin, establishes distinct cookie values, proves metadata/value authority separation, restarts the cookies service and proves actual cookie values remain engine-authoritative and context-isolated.
S3B writes deterministic localStorage in both contexts, clears one authorized context/origin through browser.site-data/0.1 and proves the other context remains unchanged.
Killing downloads or cookies service individually leaves direct browser navigation, tabs and durable history operational.

Existing Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices and All evidence remains green locally, and the required hosted master run is named separately.
After fresh evidence and explicit apply confirmation, GRACE may add dedicated downloads and cookies/site-data modules and verification projections; M1.3 remains Active.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names service-contract compatibility fixtures, download durable-intent and incomplete-outcome recovery tests, no-path artifact handoff and independent blob-read authority, cookie metadata/value authority separation, secret redaction, cross-context isolation, site-data clear isolation, service restart/failure isolation, real provider S3B evidence and a successful hosted master run. Local and hosted evidence are reported separately.

Assumptions.Assumption: C-BROWSER-TABS-HISTORY-SERVICES-20260901 remains applied and archived before this change's plan is approved or executed.
Browser Contract v1.0 and the accepted M1.2 provider architecture remain valid and are consumed rather than reopened by this service slice.

The generic external-plugin blob mechanism delivered in M1.2 can represent completed download artifacts without leaking browser-provider filesystem paths; if a reusable public generic blob-reference DTO is missing, the plan may add one generically rather than introducing a browser-specific host path.
Existing engine.cookies/0.1 and engine.storage/0.1 are sufficient for the initial service-mediated cookie inspection/mutation and origin storage clear operations.
Existing download primitives are sufficient for engine operation control, while a safer artifact-completion handoff may require an additive or separately versioned experimental engine primitive.
Exact physical service persistence schemas are chosen in the separately approved implementation plan while preserving the source-of-truth rules defined here.
Request-policy/adblock, diagnostics/search and final S3 closure remain separately governed follow-on changes.
